faq.a: Talatu is associated with the Arabic form ثَلَاثَة, whose core sense is talatu; third-born (hausa form).

faq.q: What is the origin of Talatu?
faq.a: Talatu is associated with Arabic. Talatu is the Hausa form of Arabic ثَلَاثَة (Thalātha), meaning 'third', used as a female given name.
Yes — the underlying form ثَلَاثَة is Arabic.
Talatu can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Talatu should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Thalātha is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Talatu mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Talatu is rendered ثلاثہ and carries the sense ثلاثہ، تیسرا.

faq.q: What does Talatu mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Talatu is rendered ثلاثه and carries the sense ثلاثه، سوم.
A romanized syllable approximation is ta-la-tu. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Talatu?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Talatu, talatu. Script forms are ثلاثه, ثلاثہ, ثَلَاثَة, तलातु.

faq.q: Is Talatu a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
